description:
### 🚀 **Composio Saturdays — Build, Share & Connect!**

Welcome to **Composio Saturdays**, a relaxed weekly meetup for developers, builders, and AI enthusiasts who are exploring the future of AI agents and integrations with **Composio.dev** — the platform that empowers AI agents and LLMs to interact with real-world tools and workflows.
Whether you’re just getting started or shipping production-ready agents, this event is your space to learn, create, share, and collaborate with others in the ecosystem.
**What to Expect:**
✨ **Show & Tell** – Demo what you’ve built with Composio or tools that work alongside it.
🛠 **Hands-On Sessions** – Pair up to build integrations, troubleshoot toolchains, and explore new agent workflows.
💡 **Knowledge Exchange** – Tips, tricks, and best practices for integrating AI agents into real-world apps.
🤝 **Community Networking** – Meet fellow builders, share ideas, and find collaborators for your next project.
**Who Should Join:**
Developers, architects, product builders, and anyone curious about agentic AI, automation, and practical integrations with platforms like Composio.
**Why Attend:**
Composio makes connecting intelligent agents to external tools simpler and more reliable — and Composio Saturdays is your weekly chance to level up with peers. Whether you're automating workflows or crafting production-ready systems, this meetup helps you turn ideas into action.

name: AI Philly Hack Night
description:
**AI tools are only as useful as the workflows around them.** AI Skill Share is a working session for people who want to get better results from the tools they already use, whether that is ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code, or something else. See the setups people rely on, the mistakes they learned from, and the small changes that can turn a generic AI tool into a more reliable collaborator.

Bring your laptop and something interesting to share: a skill, a project instruction file, a useful rule or hook, a workflow that needs a second opinion, or an introduction to yourself. We will trade tactics, open up our configurations, and leave with concrete upgrades to try. You do not need to be an expert; the point is to learn alongside people doing real work with AI.

**What you'll learn:**

* How to turn one-off AI chats into repeatable workflows with better instructions and context
* How other people use skills, rules, hooks, and AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md files in practice
* How to diagnose a frustrating AI workflow and identify the next improvement to try

**Who should attend:**

* Anyone who wants more useful, consistent results from AI tools
* Builders, operators, and power users with a workflow or configuration worth sharing
* Beginners who want practical guidance from people using AI on real projects

(CS)²AI Online™: Security Lifecycles of Connected Power Infrastructure
description:
[https://events.zoom.us/ev/Akgd1vdEBM3_-dVIIC984km2rdNba4A7BSm8oQ3Acj8AMaAqEuiG~AgGQltEj_HyS7hzBVFo65QjDQHd2E-V1ve9fe5tBu5wSeD96KYTH_bDG5GJkbKM7mTSe4ZhY8-zItF2ZDowp-8QxwA](https://events.zoom.us/ev/Akgd1vdEBM3_-dVIIC984km2rdNba4A7BSm8oQ3Acj8AMaAqEuiG~AgGQltEj_HyS7hzBVFo65QjDQHd2E-V1ve9fe5tBu5wSeD96KYTH_bDG5GJkbKM7mTSe4ZhY8-zItF2ZDowp-8QxwA)

The power industry has largely solved the question of whether critical power assets should be connected. UPS systems, PDUs, and power management platforms are now routinely integrated with cloud services, remote support, and operational analytics. The harder question is whether these assets are deployed in a way that justifies the trust being placed in them. Even when products are Secure by Design and Secure by Default, commissioning and integration decisions often determine the real cybersecurity outcome. Yet these activities are frequently led by teams focused on operational performance and uptime rather than cyber risk. This session examines why commissioning may be the most important security event in a power asset's lifecycle and outlines practical approaches for establishing security from day one through secure commissioning, secure-by-deployment principles, and lifecycle risk management.

Join our ICS/OT Cybersecurity star Mike Holcomb and Power specialist Saltanat Mashirova for this in-depth talk, and be sure to bring your questions for her!

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

name: Adapting Your Data Strategy for AI
description:
***PLEASE REGISTER ON THE [WEBSITE](https://damaphila.starchapter.com/meetinginfo.php?id=50&ts=1782589865) TO OBTAIN ACCESS TO THE BULDING.***

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the industry, and successful AI needs a strong data foundation. When building your Data Strategy, it can be challenging to balance when to embrace AI and when the foundational aspects of data management, business intelligence, and data governance come into play. This presentation will include how to balance both innovation and foundation with practical, business-focused approaches to building an effective strategy and roadmap.
Topics include:

* Prioritizing AI and Analytics Use Cases
* Aligning AI with Data Management and Data Governance
* Building the Right Team - Roles and Responsibilities
* Developing an Effective Roadmap

**Donna Burbank** will be speaking on this topic. A recognized industry expert in data management with over 25 years of experience helping organizations enrich their business opportunities through data. She is currently the Managing Director of Global Data Strategy, Ltd., where she assists organizations around the globe in driving value from their data. Donna speaks regularly at industry conferences, she has co-authored several books on Data Management, and is a regular contributor to industry publications.
**Securing Your Data for AI**
**Session Description**
AI changes what enterprise data does. Beyond reporting and analytics, data now directly shapes model behavior, retrieval, recommendations, automation, and agent actions — making data governance a security concern. This session uses LLM04 2026: Data and Model Poisoning as an industry reference point to examine how poisoning risk enters through untrusted sources, manipulated content, stale knowledge, unsafe feedback loops, and AI-accessible data that is treated as more authoritative than it should be. The session will connect these risks to the governance controls required to secure data for AI systems.
**Additional Topics**

* How AI expands the enterprise data attack surface
* How poisoned or manipulated content affects RAG retrieval and recommendations
* How compromised fine-tuning sets and feedback loops degrade model behavior
* Source trust, provenance, and authority for AI-accessible data
* Ingestion controls and lifecycle management for AI pipelines
* Vulnerability identification and testing specific to AI data flows
* Mapping LLM04 2026 to practical data governance decisions

**Mark Roxberry** will be speaking on the topics. He is a trusted consultant in AI security and intelligent systems architecture with over 20 years of experience helping organizations navigate the intersection of data, risk, and emerging AI. He is Principal Consultant for Security and Intelligent Solutions at Database Solutions Inc. and holds CISSP and CEH certifications. Mark works with clients across healthcare, gaming, financial services, and other regulated industries. He leads the OWASP HACTU8 AI security testing project and the OWASP LLM04 Working Group, speaks regularly on AI governance and secure architecture, and focuses on making enterprise AI capabilities useful, testable, and governable in production environments.

**ETL was the beginning, but orchestration continues to evolve. Hear first-hand from data engineers at leading companies shipping production AI workflows on Airflow.**

Join us September 16 for production stories from engineering leaders who've done it, learn hands-on tips for doing the same, and get a first look at where orchestration is going next.

**What to Expect**

* **Real Orchestration Stories:** Hear from engineering teams running AI in production. No pilots, no prototypes.
* **Practical Orchestration Patterns:** Learn practical orchestration patterns: from MLOps and AI inference to context engineering and what's coming next.
* **See What’s Next:** Get a first look at what's new from Astronomer including features built for AI workloads at scale.

**Get AI Certified with Airflow**
Join Airflow expert Marc Lamberti, creator of Data with Marc, for a preparation crash course for the New Astronomer Certified AI Orchestration Fundamentals exam. Get your questions answered live, plus you'll get a discount code to take the certification for free ($150 value).
